chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hakam ibn Miskeen, from Muhammad ibn Marwan who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There comes to be upon the man, sixty or seventy years, Allah not Accepting a Salat from him'. I said, 'And how can that be?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Because he washes what Allah Commanded for the wiping'.
ai.seo_question: Why might a person's prayers not be accepted despite praying for decades?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights the critical distinction between washing and wiping (masah) the feet in ablution, a key point of divergence between Shia and Sunni jurisprudence. He illustrates that even decades of consistent prayer can be rendered invalid if this fundamental ritual detail is overlooked, emphasizing the precision required in following divine commands. This underscores the Shia view that the method of wiping, rather than washing, the feet is the authentic practice prescribed in the Quran.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Al Hakam Bin Miskeen, from Muhammad Bin Marwan who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘There comes to be upon the man, sixty or seventy years, Allahazwj not Accepting a Salaat from him’. I said, ‘And how can that be?’ Heasws said: ‘Because he washes what Allahazwj Commanded for the wiping’.
en.sarwar: 9. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from al-Hakam ibn Miskin from Muhammad ibn Marwan who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘One may live for sixty or seventy years while Allah has not accepted not even one of his Salah (prayer).’ I (the narrator) then asked, ‘How can that happen?’
